title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Bolsonaro edges past Lula in Brazil
preheader: The far-right senator won 47.1% in the first round and will face Lula again on October 25.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Monday, October 05, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 7 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: Brazil's election goes to a runoff as Bolsonaro edges past Lula
stories.why_important: Flávio Bolsonaro won 47.1% of the vote to Lula's 45% in Sunday's first round. They face a runoff on October 25, and if Bolsonaro wins, Brazil becomes the latest Latin American country to swing right. That would have big effects for the Amazon and regional alliances.
stories.what_overlooked: The first round also showed strong support for Bolsonaro's far-right movement. It has not promised to accept a runoff defeat, so some fear a repeat of the 2023 coup attempt.
stories.prediction: Lula and Bolsonaro will begin televised debates next week. Whether Lula can win back centrist support will decide the runoff.

stories.story_title: Spain calls snap election after housing protests
stories.why_important: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called early elections for November 29 after Parliament rejected his housing decrees. The vote could end one of Europe's last left-wing governments as the far-right gains across the continent.
stories.what_overlooked: The housing crisis has fueled protests across Spain. The opposition People's Party has not yet offered a clear alternative, leaving room for the far-right Vox to gain.
stories.prediction: Sánchez will try to pass a new housing package before the election; if he fails, Vox may gain more in the polls.

stories.story_title: US pulls B-1 bombers from UK base after terror plot
stories.why_important: The US Air Force removed all B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in England after a suspected terror plot. The base supported strikes on Iran, and the quick pullout suggests a serious security threat that could raise US-Iran tensions.
stories.what_overlooked: British police found petrol in vans near the base but no explosives. They are still investigating, and it's unclear who was behind the plot.
stories.prediction: US officials will likely announce new security measures at European bases. Any link to Iran would cause a diplomatic crisis.
